provenance: PR #33 R1 (HIGH): `certify = bool(parsed["certify"])` treated ANY truthy JSON value -- including the strings "false"/"no", present in a completion actually shaped like a formatting slip a real model can make -- as certify=True, inverting the fail-closed guarantee that is this milestone's entire purpose. None of the 8 cases committed in the first round exercised `live_judge()`'s real parsing path at all -- all eight used `stub_judge`, which bypasses `json.loads`/fence-stripping/the certify extraction entirely, so the code that actually runs in production was completely ungraded (the reviewer's structural note, not just the line-level bug). WATCHED RED FIRST against the pre-fix `bool()` coercion: the string-typed/numeric/null scenarios above all reported `got: certify` (the exact inversion) instead of `reject`. This probe mocks ONLY `urllib.request.urlopen` -- judge.py's actual `json.loads`, fence-stripping and extraction code runs unmodified -- with a fake (non-functional) API key so the call proceeds past the missing-key guard, and a uuid4 nonce per scenario so a stale cache entry from an earlier suite run can never substitute for actually exercising the parser. Fixed by replacing the coercion with strict identity (`parsed["certify"] is True`), the form the reviewer named as preferred over trying to parse truthiness: every value other than the literal JSON `true` is a reject, not an exception (a genuinely absent `certify` key still raises via `KeyError`, caught the same as any other malformed response). PR #33 R2/R3 (MEDIUM, repair round 2): the strict is-True check closes the over-certify direction (R1) but silently introduces the opposite ceiling -- a provider response of {"certify": "true"} (a formatting slip in the CERTIFYING direction) now fails closed too, and no scenario here pinned it and no document declared it. This scenario was NOT watched red: the strict check already rejects it correctly (parsed['certify'] is True -> False for the string 'true'), so there was no code defect to fix in this direction -- only a coverage/documentation gap, closed here (the scenario) and in docs/support-matrix.md D26 (the declared cost, same spirit as D22's aggregate-guard false-refusal row: a real, priced cost with no fixture demonstrating it in the wild, because nobody here can observe what the live model actually emits).
